title: Microsoft Agent 365: registry sync from external AI platforms
summary: Hold: the observability control path omits the step to edit the connection, and the licensing discussion overlooks Microsoft's published feature-availability table. Most operational details match the documentation, but the briefing also needs to acknowledge the registry-sync preview designation and a platform-specific difference in how the first synchronization starts.

claims.claim: Synchronization does not currently run on a schedule.

claims.claim: After saving a connection, an administrator must select Sync agents to start synchronization.

claims.fix: Qualify the initial-sync instruction wherever repeated: 'The general Connected platforms guide says to select Sync agents after saving. The Databricks Genie guide says saving starts the first synchronization automatically; later runs use Sync agents.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/connected-platforms-databricks-genie#synchronize-agents, which states 'When you save the connection, the details pane opens and starts the first synchronization.'

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Removing an agent from the source platform does not guarantee its automatic removal from the registry.
claims.quote: Synchronization doesn't currently guarantee that an agent removed from the source platform is automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.claim: Registry sync does not add code-level Agent 365 capabilities.
claims.quote: Registry sync doesn't add code-level capabilities. It provides visibility and governance for agents you don't build or host yourself.

claims.claim: Supported connected-platform agents appear alongside other agents in the organization's shared inventory.
claims.quote: Agent 365 can synchronize supported agents from connected platforms into the Microsoft 365 agent registry, where they appear with other agents in the organization's inventory.

claims.claim: Registry coverage depends on the platform and does not guarantee that every source agent is included.
claims.quote: Coverage depends on the connected platform and the agents it exposes, so a registry entry represents the supported information available from that source - not a guarantee that every agent on the platform is included.

claims.where: Why it matters: agents the admin center does not otherwise list
claims.claim: Agents built on Bedrock, Vertex AI or Agentforce are not otherwise listed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 external agents automatically discovered without registry sync. Opened guidance/connected-platforms and developer/choose-integration-option; read connect-existing-agents and developer/agent-365-sdk search excerpts. No exclusive inventory route is stated.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Registry sync brings supported agents from Bedrock, Vertex AI and Agentforce into the Microsoft 365 agent registry.' The existing Connected platforms citation supports this narrower statement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: optional delete permission
claims.claim: Writing to the source platform is limited to explicit administrator removal of a synced agent using a separate optional delete permission.
claims.quote: The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent, which requires a separate, optional delete permission that you can choose not to grant.
claims.fix: Add the qualification: 'For Databricks Genie, Can Manage is required for activity collection and also permits moving an agent to the trash when an administrator removes it in Agent 365.'
